Mohamed Salah and the ghosts of Egypt’s ‘golden generation’

Salah has previously taken flak from Egypt’s fans. Now he leads an undefeated team into the round of 16 against Argentina — and a nation is daring to believe again.

Patricia Sabga· 4h ago

Mohamed Salah celebrates after Egypt beat Australia in the last 32 of the 2026 World Cup

For some Egyptian football fans, watching Mohamed Salah qualify with Egypt for two World Cups in 2018 and 2026 will never make up for the fact that the “golden generation” did not get their shot in 2006, 2010 or 2014.

“It is unfair to compare the two generations,” Ahmed Elshiekh, a former national team player who now covers the World Cup for Modern MTI TV, told Al Jazeera. “The golden generation did everything but get to the World Cup. They beat Italy when they were world champions. The draw was just unkind to them.”


Salah is the captain and leader of the current generation. He won every trophy on offer during a glittering nine-year career at Liverpool that made him the highest-scoring foreigner in Premier League history. Given his status, it is perhaps no surprise that he shouldered the blame for an AFCON drought stretching back to 2010.

“This Egypt team is better than any we have seen in years — yet is still remarkably fragile.”

THIERY HENRY

World cup winner with france ‘02

Salah finds form under Hassan

Instead of falling out with Salah, manager Hossam Hassan became joined at the hip with his captain. If anyone understood the pressure, it was Hassan — who had lived it before, with the added weight of having crossed the Cairo divide from Al Ahly to bitter rivals Zamalek.

The failures compounded: the 2021 AFCON final lost to Senegal on penalties, then a World Cup playoff against the same opponent lost the same way. In the first shootout Salah, listed fifth, never got his kick. In the second he went first — and missed.

​

To soothe the pain, fans clung to the team crowned African champions in 2006, 2008 and 2010 — led by Mohamed Aboutrika, as famous for his “Sympathise with Gaza” T-shirt as for his immaculate first touch.

Photograpgh by Sarah Chen, Al jazeera

Egypt qualified for 2026 undefeated, winning eight of ten. A second-half comeback against New Zealand delivered the nation’s first-ever World Cup win. Salah left the Iran game with a hamstring injury — then played all 120 minutes of the shootout win over Australia, converting his kick with a Panenka.

Afterwards, Aboutrika — now a beIN Sports analyst — passed the baton. When goalscorer Emam Ashour said he dreamed of being “half as good” as Aboutrika, the great man replied: “You are better than me. You’ve scored two goals in a World Cup.”

Salah, asked once more who is the greatest Egyptian player of all time, deferred again: “There is absolutely no discussion.” On Tuesday, against Argentina, he can end it anyway.
